recommendations.what: Measure how redundant v1's answers are (share of shown items sharing a file or a slice with another shown item), and add an MMR-style or facility-location term only if that share is large.
recommendations.from_theory: MMR (Carbonell and Goldstein 1998); submodular packers (2607.00725, RCD, AdaGReS).
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing at present: v1 has no redundancy control.
recommendations.expected_effect: Small. 2607.00725 found +0.051 F1 over naive packing on one multi-hop set and null elsewhere; MMR +0.010 over naive; plain Lead beat both at 256 tokens in RCD.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Redundancy audit first (zero model tokens); if repeated structure exceeds roughly a quarter of answer items, add the term and compare recall per token paired by commit.
recommendations.verdict: trial, low priority; skip if the audit shows little repeated structure

recommendations.what: A connect operation: given 2 to 8 named entities, return the minimum Steiner tree over the typed graph with edge cost equal to minus the log of the edge's reliability (so the cheapest connection is the most probable chain), listed as indented paths with each edge's evidence line.
recommendations.from_theory: Steiner tree and prize-collecting Steiner tree (Goemans-Williamson 2-approximation; G-Retriever, AGRAG); exact Dreyfus-Wagner (about 3^k times polynomial) is feasible at 5,464 nodes; -log cost transform is standard but untested here.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Metapath returns and PPR top-k as the only way to answer 'where is the other half of this contract' and 'how does screen X reach table Y'.
recommendations.expected_effect: Targets explanation questions, not recall. Literature shows no gain over simple scoring on recall metrics and shows bare trees dropping answers (AGRAG); do not expect gains on the change-completion task.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: On tuning commits with 2 or more seed files, and on documented-chain questions available at tuning time, score evidence recall per token of the Steiner tree against PPR top-k at the same token size; add a cycle-closing expansion variant (AGRAG) as a second arm. Report only on the questions where the reference is a connecting path.
recommendations.needs_install: None for exact (write Dreyfus-Wagner in JavaScript); optional pcst_fast (pip, C++ with Python wrapper, small, builds offline on Linux) only for more than about 10 terminals.
recommendations.verdict: trial for explanation questions only; not a default retrieval method

recommendations.what: Default output format is a file-grouped tree in rank order: each file once, definitions under it, relation tags (calls, <-called_by, writes_table) with the evidence line; use natural-language 'path::Name' ids the model can paste into the next call.
recommendations.from_theory: LocAgent tree-based expansion (79.41 file Acc@5 vs JSON 76.47 vs incident 73.53, n=37, weak); my measurement (tree 0.43x and adjacency 0.61x the tokens of triples); triples not worse than prose (2402.11541); adjacency vs edge list for small models (2603.06635); copyable names (Anthropic guidance; small-agent exact-id result).
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Four output forms (paths; path plus signature; path plus range; snippet) without relation tags or evidence lines.
recommendations.expected_effect: 39 to 57 % fewer tokens per edge than triples; accuracy effect unknown, probably small for a frontier model.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Zero model tokens: tokens per fact and recall per token for tree, adjacency, triples and JSON on the same selected set. With model tokens: a reading test (no agent loop) of 25 documented-chain or typed-lookup questions x 4 formats x 3 repeats, about 300 short calls of roughly 300 to 2,000 tokens each, so about 0.3 to 0.6 million tokens; question set must be hand-checked, not extractor-derived.
recommendations.verdict: adopt as default pending the reading test

recommendations.what: A three-tool surface: find (exact name then BM25 over symbols, paths and doc text; at most 8 one-line results), around (entity, intent enum of impact, uses, contract, rules, tests, history; default 1,000 tokens, hard 2,000; builder output; footer that names what was omitted by relation kind and slice and which argument would include it), connect (as above, at most 12 lines). A fourth tool, notes (stored conclusions with a validity flag), only if the knowledge-layer lane delivers it. Each definition about 60 to 100 tokens (purpose, when to use, limits; no examples). No query-language tool and no next-page command.
recommendations.from_theory: LocAgent 3 tools and its ablation (entry point 19 points, traversal about 2); SWE-agent ACI (summarised search 18.0 vs iterative 12.0; mid-sized window; 50-result withhold); small-agent study caps (50 lines, 4,000 characters); CypherBench and CodexGraph against query writing; Anthropic consolidation and token-efficiency guidance; 'Docs to Descriptions' and 'smelly descriptions' on wording; re-read arithmetic (section 4.5).
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: The scripted query set the v1 harness used (typed queries through the harness, never through a model).
recommendations.expected_effect: Lets an agent get an exact answer in roughly 1,000 tokens instead of a search-and-read sequence; saving depends on adoption. Cost side: definitions are paid every call.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Parts that need no model: answer tokens, recall per token and p50/p90 output size per tool on tuning seeds, and a count of how often the footer's narrowing argument would recover an omitted reference. Parts that need an agent pilot (owner decision, model tokens): per-run tool-call and server-connection logs, total tokens with and without definitions loaded (to measure D x T), success on replayed tuning commits, and a steering arm (hook or short file) kept separate from the tool arm.
recommendations.needs_install: None beyond the owner's MCP or tool-registration choice; no new libraries. The agent pilot needs model tokens; the first test's 31 versus about 695 tokens per lookup and the harness's 113 to 123k-token average calls suggest hundreds of thousands to a few million tokens per arm, which I could not verify.
recommendations.verdict: adopt as the design to test; do not claim it works until the agent pilot

recommendations.what: Do not build: a model-written query language tool (Cypher or SQL), ToG-style multi-call LLM traversal with an LLM pruner, LLM-written community summaries, or a trained subgraph scorer.
recommendations.from_theory: CypherBench (60.18 % to 61.58 % best, under 20 % below 10B parameters) and CodexGraph (+35 % tokens, 1.95 % vs 9.34 % on a weak model); ToG 11.6 calls and 7,069 tokens vs 2 calls and 231 to 521 for prepared designs; GraphRAG vs plain retrieval on detail questions; SubgraphRAG's learned scorer needs supervised training and its text did not state the training set size in what I read.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing in v1 (these are options that were discussed, not built).
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids cost and failure modes; at 10x to 100x size summaries and learned scorers become more defensible but still need task-specific evidence.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Not tested; revisit only if a fixed-tool arm shows a specific ceiling the proposed method addresses.

recommendations.what: Swap the Louvain community prior for Leiden (or drop the prior in favour of the existing slice folders).
recommendations.from_theory: Leiden guarantees connected communities where Louvain can return disconnected ones (Traag, Waltman, van Eck 2019); k-core hierarchies (2603.05207) argue modularity methods are unstable on sparse graphs.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: The Louvain community prior in the fused variants.
recommendations.expected_effect: Small; slices already give the grouping, and the evidence is on text corpora with different degree structure.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Rerun the fused variant with Leiden partitions on the tuning split; compare recall-versus-tokens curves paired by commit; also compare against the slice-folder partition.
recommendations.needs_install: igraph and leidenalg or python-igraph (pip wheels, tens of MB, offline on Linux).

earlier_research_missed: Round 1 (lane-agent-graphs.txt) said to cap output in tokens and prefer precision but gave no method for cutting a ranked list to a budget, no cost-per-item model and no stopping rule; this lane supplies the knapsack and submodular formulations and the value-density stop, and notes v1 is exactly Aider's rank-prefix rule.

Round 1 and round 2 both left 'does ranked 2 to 3 hop closure computed by the tool beat leaving chaining to the model' open; the knowledge-graph question answering papers (ToG, GCR, RoG, SubgraphRAG) bear on it: prepared or constrained retrieval used 1 to 2 calls and 231 to 521 tokens per question against 11.6 calls and 7,069 tokens for LLM-driven traversal, though readers differ so the comparison is not controlled.
Round 1 ruled out LLM-written Cypher on CodexGraph evidence alone and cited no accuracy data for query writing; CypherBench gives 60.18 % to 61.58 % best and under 20 % below 10B parameters.

Round 1 recommended returning paths, signatures and relation lines with no format evidence and did not report LocAgent's output-format table (tree 79.41, JSON 76.47, incident 73.53 file Acc@5 on 37 samples); neither round measured the token cost of formats on this graph (tree 0.43x, adjacency 0.61x, JSON 1.07x, sentences 1.15x relative to triples).

Neither round covered tool-definition cost or description wording as a design variable: 58 tools about 55,000 tokens, 49 % to 74 % accuracy with tool search, selection probability gains of +11.6 points for functionality wording, +5.85 points success at +67 % steps for richer descriptions.

Neither round reported SWE-agent's controlled results on output design: summarised search 18.0 % vs paging 12.0 %, a 100-line window 18.0 % vs 30 lines 14.3 % vs whole file 12.7 %, and the 50-result withhold rule.

The round 1 and round 2 figure that each extra hop multiplies the odds of correct localisation by 0.47 to 0.55 comes from a superseded version of arXiv 2610.33958; I read v2 (9 November 2026) and found no per-hop table or chaining count in the text I could read (11,175 characters unread), and the 'about half the gain from exact ids' claim is more accurately a 27 to 45 % shrinkage for the two smallest Qwen3 models.

Neither round considered hierarchy-aware (tree or multiple-choice knapsack) selection, which is the natural fit for a graph whose nodes are a file and its symbols; I found no source applying it to code, so it is an unproven inference.

Neither round examined Steiner or PCST evidence beyond naming it; the reading shows the only ablation of the Steiner step is a tree-versus-expansion comparison in AGRAG and PCST plus top-25 versus top-25 alone in Ex-GraphRAG, and that SubgraphRAG reaches 89.80 Hit with no graph optimisation.
could_not_verify: Primary texts of Nemhauser, Wolsey and Fisher 1978; Khuller, Moss and Naor 1999; Sviridenko 2004; Leskovec et al. KDD 2007; Goemans and Williamson 1995; Dreyfus and Wagner 1971; tree-knapsack papers: guarantees and complexities came from search snippets, secondary papers and one 2020 arXiv paper (2008.05391, abstract page).
Lin and Bilmes 2010 and Carbonell and Goldstein 1998: abstract pages only. Johnson, Minkoff and Phillips 2000: not found. Hegde, Indyk and Schmidt 2015: snippets and the pcst_fast README only.

PDFs did not parse through the fetch tool; I used arXiv HTML. Tails were unread: G-Retriever 953 characters, SubgraphRAG 33,865, ToG 30,296, RoG 8,357, GCR 24,122, AGRAG 44,156, CypherBench 38,887, SWE-agent 104,413, arXiv 2610.33958 11,175, arXiv 2602.14878 133,070, arXiv 2511.10234 6,397, the k-core paper 25,976. Ablations or limitations in those tails are not covered.

Fetch extractions contradicted themselves in places: ToG Tables 1 and 2 on CWQ and its 8.4 % and 15.1 % average drops versus my table subtraction (7.3 and 13.7 points); GCR's stated 9.1 % gain versus its table; RAG-MCP 49 % versus 'over 50 %' and garbled stress-test range; Anthropic 85 % versus about 89 %; AdaGReS derivation constant. I report table values.

Neo4j Text2Cypher benchmark numbers, the TACL 2026 GraphRAG verbalisation paper, the JSAI 2025 JSON-versus-triples report, KAPING verbalisation results, PathRAG win rates, and the G-Retriever versus SubgraphRAG table (53.41 and 73.46) could not be mapped to metrics: snippets only.

No source tested budgeted selection, hierarchy-aware selection or stop rules on a code graph for an agent; all selection evidence is on text passages, knowledge-graph QA or summarisation with readers from 3B to GPT-4 class, so transfer to a frontier coding agent is untested. The 2026 submodular packer papers are unreplicated preprints.

The 31-versus-695 token lookup figures, the held-out precision at 10 items (0.26 to 0.28), the 113 to 123k average call size and the paired SD of 0.263 came from earlier notes of this project, not from my measurements. My own measurements use v1's regex tokenizer (a model tokenizer was not available), cover symbol seeds with at least 8 edges for the format comparison (64 seeds, edges capped at 30 per seed), and do not test how well a model reads any format.
Definition token sizes for the proposed tools (about 120 each) are my assumption; whether the owner's total-token metric counts cached definitions at face value was not checked.
I did not run any model, so nothing here shows the proposed tool interface raises an agent's success or lowers its total tokens on this repository; the agent pilot is the test.

time_incremental.summary: Time, cached conclusions and invalidation are covered by four old, well-documented bodies of theory: incremental view maintenance (counting, delete-and-rederive, DBSP, differential dataflow), provenance (lineage, semirings, why-not), truth maintenance (Doyle 1979, de Kleer 1986) and build-system incremental computation (Build Systems a la Carte, Skyframe, Salsa). For deterministic answers, recorded dependencies with verifying traces and early cutoff give the same guarantee as a Datalog maintenance engine (the served answer equals a recomputation). At this size (about 5,400 nodes, 10,800 edges per snapshot, 230 commits) the engine buys nothing: K0 answered 247 questions in 6.0 ms and a whole-graph ranking in about 14 ms. What a rule language would add is dependencies extracted from the rules instead of instrumented by hand, and a single read API plus an exhaustive single-fact mutation test gives that safety without an install. K0's hand-built "nothing else matches" patterns are predicate locks and the phantom problem (Eswaran et al. 1976), query-update independence (Blakeley et al. 1986; Levy and Sagiv 1993), why-not provenance, Skyframe's directory-listing nodes and Doyle's out-lists. A model-made conclusion breaks the two assumptions every published algorithm makes (determinism, complete recorded inputs); Build Systems a la Carte already models it as a non-deterministic task with untracked dependencies, so correctness is relaxed and early cutoff on the prose is unsound. The workable design is a ledger of typed premises (graph-query results, text hashes, absence searches with scope, document hashes), re-verified deterministically with early cutoff at the query-result level, with the prose marked suspect when a premise's result changes; the trigger must be an external diff, since model self-verification without external feedback is unreliable. For an agent resuming work, git plus memoised snapshots keyed by (commit, extractor version) already provide the temporal model: a since-view is the filtered diff of two snapshots joined to the agent's stored conclusions. I measured digest sizes on the finished test's snapshots: about 1 percent of edges change per commit (median 115, p90 645); near a random file the 1-hop digest is empty 70.5 percent of the time after about 2 commits, and the 2-hop median is 27 edges after about 8 commits and 151 after about 31. Interval stores, bitemporal tables and temporal graph databases add nothing here and only start to pay at roughly 100 times the size. No published study shows that any of this reduces an agent's tokens on code; the one agent-facing number (Copilot memory, 90 vs 83 percent merge rate) is vendor-reported with no sample size, and independent studies of stored model-written context are neutral to negative. Each recommendation therefore has a zero-model test on tuning data first.

findings.claim: For deterministic derived answers, incremental maintenance (counting, DRed, FBF, DBSP) and recorded dependencies with verifying traces and early cutoff have the same correctness criterion: the served answer equals a from-scratch recomputation. They differ in cost model and in where dependencies come from.
findings.evidence: Build Systems a la Carte Def. 3.1 (result equals recomputation) and Def. 2.1 (minimality); DBSP defines the incremental query as D o Q o I, equal to recomputation by definition, with chain rule and antijoin for stratified negation; Motik et al. prove counting, DRed and FBF correct for stratified negation and show no algorithm is optimal on all inputs for recursive rules.
findings.source: Mokhov, Mitchell, Peyton Jones ICFP 2018 (full text read); Budiu, McSherry, Ryzhyk, Tannen arXiv 2203.16684 v1 (full text read); Motik, Nenov, Piro, Horrocks AIJ 2019 (full text read)
findings.strength: THEORY (proved); engineering evidence strong for build systems, medium for IVM
findings.applies_at_this_size: Soundness result applies at any size. Speed benefit of IVM does not: K0 recompute costs about 24 microseconds per question (6.0 ms for 247) and about 14 ms per whole-graph ranking; Motik's comparison is at 12.5 to 387 million explicit facts.

findings.claim: K0's negative-dependency patterns are the known phantom problem. The same object appears under five names: predicate locks, query-update independence, why-not provenance (failed derivations), Skyframe's directory-listing node under a glob, and the out-list of a Doyle justification.
findings.evidence: Eswaran et al.: a transaction must lock a logical subset defined by a predicate because phantoms do not exist yet; Blakeley et al. give necessary and sufficient conditions for irrelevant updates to select-project-join views; Motik lists relevance of updates as a related problem (Blakeley, Elkan, Levy and Sagiv for datalog); Lee et al. rewrite Datalog with negation to record failed derivations, implemented in SQL; Skyframe makes readdir a node and globs depend on it and warns an unregistered dependency can cause incorrect builds; de Kleer describes Doyle's SL-justification as in-list and out-list.
findings.source: Eswaran et al. CACM 1976 (full text read); Blakeley, Coburn, Larson VLDB 1986 (full text read); Lee, Koehler, Ludascher, Glavic arXiv 1701.05699 and PUG arXiv 1808.05752 (read); Bazel Skyframe docs (page summary); de Kleer AIJ 1986 (full text read)
findings.strength: THEORY plus medium engineering
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes. K0 found 133 of 134 dependency cases were a new relation in another file, which is exactly this case; file-level and pattern-less fact-level policies served 6.5 and 6.8 percent stale answers (13.2 and 13.6 percent on the changing questions).

findings.claim: Provenance semirings give a formal hierarchy for what an answer rests on: why-provenance (set of contributing tuples) is coarser than polynomial how-provenance, and difference (negation) and aggregation are hard cases whose provenance is wider and not fully axiomatised.
findings.evidence: Green et al. show two output tuples with the same why-provenance but different polynomials (2s^2+rs vs 2r^2+rs) and list negation as further work; Amsterdamer, Deutch, Tannen show semiring extensions to difference violate expected axioms for some semirings and that aggregates need provenance on values.
findings.source: Green, Karvounarakis, Tannen PODS 2007 (full text read); Amsterdamer, Deutch, Tannen arXiv 1105.2255 and 1101.1110 (abstracts read)
findings.strength: THEORY
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes as explanation: K0's flat read set is lineage, which over-invalidates (88.8 percent of fact-level recomputations, 66 percent for the semantic-hash variant, returned the same answer); the whole-graph ranking has median 3,633 nodes in its dependency set, matching the aggregate case. Cost of the over-invalidation is milliseconds, not tokens.

findings.claim: Datalog was chosen for code analysis for declarativeness and automatic optimisation of large mutually recursive analyses, not for incrementality. Incremental Datalog speedups are real but measured at millions of derived tuples.
findings.evidence: Doop: same analysis 15 to 16 times faster than the BDD-based Paddle with identical results; unoptimised Datalog over 1000 times slower. FlowLog demo: retracting one fact from a 4,986,481-tuple points-to result took about 7 ms against 2.23 s recomputation (320 times); DDlog used a median 6.3 times more memory than FlowLog. Glean: 7 percent larger database, 2 to 3 percent indexing overhead, queries under 10 percent slower; incremental derivation implemented only for some query kinds.
findings.source: Bravenboer and Smaragdakis OOPSLA 2009 (full text read); Yu et al. SPLASH 2026 companion, arXiv 2607.23971 (full text read); Glean incremental blog (page summary)
findings.strength: Medium (authors' own benchmarks); Glean strong as an engineering description with no agent measurement
findings.applies_at_this_size: No. This repository's derived relations are about three orders of magnitude smaller than the FlowLog case; the declarative benefit (dependencies by construction) applies, the speed benefit does not.

findings.claim: DDlog, the main incremental Datalog compiler, is archived and read-only; FlowLog is a 2026 research prototype; Feldera (DBSP, MIT) is SQL with recursion, not Datalog, with a heavy source build; Souffle (UPL) has no incremental mode on its page.
findings.evidence: GitHub pages: vmware differential-datalog archived 13 July 2026; feldera MIT, Docker image, source build needs Rust, C++ compiler, cmake, JDK 19+, Maven, Python 3.10, Bun, Node 20 and about 13 GB; souffle-lang UPL-1.0 with interpreter and provenance listed.
findings.source: GitHub repository pages for vmware/differential-datalog, feldera/feldera, souffle-lang/souffle (page summaries)
findings.strength: Weak (page summaries, status checks)
findings.applies_at_this_size: Relevant only to the install decision, which is reject for now.

findings.claim: A model-made conclusion is a non-deterministic task with untracked dependencies; correctness must be relaxed to 'the stored value is one possible recomputation', volatile tasks cannot be cached, and deep traces require determinism. So early cutoff on the conclusion text is unsound; early cutoff on deterministic premise query results is sound.
findings.evidence: Build Systems a la Carte section 6.3 (non-determinism: result is one element of the possible results), section 6 (untracked dependencies, volatile tasks cannot be cached), section 4.2.4 (deep constructive traces with n>=2 require deterministic tasks, no early cutoff).
findings.source: Mokhov, Mitchell, Peyton Jones ICFP 2018 (full text read)
findings.strength: THEORY
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes.

findings.claim: The one production design for staleness of model-made repository facts is cite-and-verify at use: each memory has subject, fact, code citations and reason; the agent re-reads the cited locations before applying it and corrects or refreshes it. Reported benefit is outcome, not tokens, with no sample sizes.
findings.evidence: GitHub reports coding-agent PR merge rate 90 percent with memory vs 83 percent without, code-review positive feedback 77 vs 75 percent, p below 0.00001, no n; an adversarial fake-citation test with no numbers; no expiry mechanism stated in the page summary (secondary coverage claims 28 days).
findings.source: GitHub blog 'Building an agentic memory system for GitHub Copilot', 9 Jan 2026 (page summary)
findings.strength: Weak (vendor, no sample size, no tokens)
findings.applies_at_this_size: Design applies; effect size unknown.

findings.claim: A model's own list of what it relied on cannot serve as the premise set, and re-checking by the model alone is unreliable; the trigger and evidence for a re-check must be deterministic.
findings.evidence: Up to 57 percent of citations in attributed answers are unfaithful (post-rationalisation); without external feedback LLM self-correction does not help and can hurt; GPT-4 self-critique collapsed on three tasks while a sound external verifier gave significant gains.
findings.source: Wallat et al. arXiv 2412.18004; Huang et al. arXiv 2310.01798; Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati arXiv 2402.08115 (abstracts read)
findings.strength: Medium to weak (independent, abstract-level, 2023 to 2024 models, not code)
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes.

findings.claim: Stored model-written context has not been shown to save tokens on code; independent studies are neutral to negative. Invalidation granularity matters in the same direction as K0's file-vs-fact result.
findings.evidence: ETH Zurich: LLM-written context files about 20 percent more cost, no significant gain; VibeMemBench: 11 of 12 pairings did not beat memory off; SWE Context Bench: wrongly chosen summary 22.22 vs 26.26 percent baseline; Invalidation Contracts: row-level invalidation recovered 29 to 33 percent of token cost on 4 of 7 models while table-level dropped first-try success to 0 percent on 5 of 7.
findings.source: Earlier lane (ETH Zurich, VibeMemBench, SWE Context Bench, read); Wu and Canedo arXiv 2609.00243 (abstract read)
findings.strength: Medium for the first three; weak for Invalidation Contracts
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes; sets the prior that conclusion caching helps tokens only if reuse is frequent, which is untested.

findings.claim: Commits already are transaction time and git is the version store; bitemporal modelling collapses to one axis for facts plus a second axis for stored conclusions (when concluded, with which graph version). A snapshot is a pure function of (commit, extractor version), so it is a cache entry, not a second database.
findings.evidence: Datomic as-of/since/history; XTDB valid time vs system time; SQL:2011 period tables; DBSP stream of snapshots and differences; differential computation allows versions from a partial order, which fits a commit DAG; Build Systems a la Carte treats the tool version as an untracked dependency that must be part of the key.
findings.source: Datomic and XTDB docs (page summaries); Kulkarni and Michels SIGMOD Record 2012 (summaries only); Budiu et al. 2022; McSherry et al. CIDR 2013 (full text read)
findings.strength: Engineering designs and theory; no agent measurements
findings.applies_at_this_size: Yes. Interval stores and DeltaGraph-style indexes pay only at scale: 190 snapshots are 778 MB; full snapshots for 10 times the commits would be about 9.4 GB (my arithmetic), at which point snapshots should be a rebuildable cache or share structure.

findings.claim: Measured size of a what-changed digest on the finished test's snapshots: about 1 percent of edges change per commit; near a random file the digest is usually empty after one or two commits and small after about 8.
findings.evidence: 189 first-parent-tree steps: edges changed median 115, p90 645, max 1,703 (excluding co_changed: 81, 512, 1,448); nodes median 26. findings.claim: Time-respecting paths and interval-stamped temporal graph models exist with polynomial algorithms but have no demonstrated value for predicting code changes; recency helps co-change ranking modestly and static file proximity helps as much.

HistoRank on 10 systems: MAP 0.05 to 0.37; recency best on 3, file proximity best on 6, similarity on 1; recency beat support and confidence ranking (p=0.04) but not file proximity or similarity; confidence ranking worst on all ten.

recommendations.what: R1. Conclusion ledger with typed premises: structured claim (a deterministic query plus its answer where possible), hard premise set (graph-query reads with result hash and K0 pattern deps; text reads with path, range, content hash and symbol; absence searches with scope and result hash; document hashes with section anchor), declared witness set as a hint only, environment key (model, prompt hash, extractor version, graph version), status VALID / VALID-BY-CUTOFF / SUSPECT-WEAK / SUSPECT / UNVERIFIABLE, and a premise-to-conclusion index to find suspects after a commit. Premises are recorded at query-result granularity so early cutoff works on deterministic results; nothing is deleted.
recommendations.from_theory: Doyle JTMS justifications with in-list and out-list; de Kleer ATMS labels; Build Systems a la Carte verifying traces and the relaxed correctness for non-deterministic tasks; lineage; Copilot cite-and-verify (vendor).
recommendations.expected_effect: Stale conclusions are never served as facts; premise revalidation is milliseconds and zero model tokens when recorded query results are unchanged. No token effect is predicted; the benefit is bounded by how often conclusions are reused, which is untested.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: (i) Zero-model: replay the tuning-window steps using the 250 K0 questions as stand-in conclusions; hard-set validation must give 0 stale; report over-invalidation per premise class. (ii) Small pilot on agent findings taken from existing session transcripts: label each 'still true at commit C+k' (deterministic re-derivation where the claim is a query, strong model plus human check otherwise); compare precision and recall of three triggers (hard set changed, declared witness changed, either). Reject a trigger that misses a non-trivial share of false findings or flags nearly everything. Held-out commits stay sealed.
recommendations.needs_install: Nothing; plain Node on the existing K0 recorder.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing; v1 stores no conclusions. It builds on K0's recorder as the premise layer.

recommendations.what: R2. Static kind-level relevance filter in front of K0's fact-level check: per question program, the set of node and edge kinds it can read, derived from the program text; an update that adds or removes no fact of those kinds cannot change the answer.
recommendations.from_theory: Irrelevant-update detection (Blakeley, Coburn, Larson 1986); query-update independence (Levy and Sagiv 1993).
recommendations.expected_effect: Cheap validation without touching the graph for narrow programs. Indicative selectivity from my reading of the programs: no add or remove in the settings kind in 72.0 percent of 189 steps, migrations 65.6, route-client 64.6, constrains 88.4, but only 21.2 for the calls family. No token effect; stale rate zero by construction if the read API is the only path.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Rerun K0's replay with this policy on tuning snapshots; stale must be 0; report hit rate and validation time against fact (0.31 ms per snapshot) and fact_sem (0.79 ms). Reject if validation is no faster or any stale answer appears.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing; adds a tier before the K0 fact policy.

recommendations.what: R3. Enforce a single read API for all question programs (lint over the program files) and run an exhaustive single-fact mutation test of the recorder: at one tuning snapshot, remove every node and edge, and add a sample of plausible edges per kind, and for each of the 250 questions check that validation says 'valid' only when the recomputed answer is equal.
recommendations.from_theory: Skyframe's unregistered-dependency warning; query-update independence solved by enumeration on a small instance; Build Systems a la Carte correctness definition.
recommendations.expected_effect: Finds any recorder gap that real history did not exercise; K0 predicts zero stale for its nine programs. Cost of the order of two minutes (about 22 thousand removals times 250 questions at about 24 microseconds each; my arithmetic).
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: The test is the experiment: stale count must be 0 for fact-level policies and any nonzero is a program or recorder bug; also report over-invalidation per kind.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: The reliance on real history to exercise the recorder.

recommendations.what: R4. Treat graph snapshots as a memo table keyed by (commit, extractor version); provide a since-view as the diff of the agent's last-seen snapshot and the current snapshot (or working-tree overlay), filtered to the k-hop neighbourhood of the agent's anchors with hubs not expanded, ordered by distance, capped, plus the list of the agent's stored conclusions whose premises intersect the diff. Do not build an interval store or a bitemporal store.
recommendations.from_theory: DBSP stream of snapshots and differences; Datomic since; Glean stacked databases; differential computation (versions from a partial order) as the principled route if a commit DAG is ever needed; git as the version store.
recommendations.expected_effect: Measured digest sizes on the finished snapshots: median 0 to 2 changed edges near a file after about 2 commits, 27 after about 8, 151 after about 31 (2-hop). Token effect not measured.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: On tuning pairs, compare the digest's token size and content with the scripted baseline git diff --stat between the two commits restricted to the same neighbourhood's directories; measure the share of the next commit's changed files that fall inside the digest's 2-hop set against a recency-only list. Reject if the digest is not smaller than the scripted diff for the same information or finds the next changed files no more often than recency alone.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing in v1; adds a retrieval mode.

recommendations.what: R5. Working-tree overlay in the Glean style: units are files; base is the cached HEAD snapshot; changed files are re-extracted and their base units hidden; derived cross-file facts (URL to route, imports, route prefixes) are re-derived for affected units; answers are validated against the overlay.
recommendations.from_theory: Glean incremental databases with unit ownership and derived-fact ownership (Meta's measured overhead: about 7 percent size, 2 to 3 percent indexing).
recommendations.expected_effect: Answers reflect the agent's own uncommitted edits within seconds instead of the 5 s full rebuild per commit.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Apply random uncommitted edits to files at tuning commits; the overlay graph must equal a full rebuild of the edited tree; report time against 5 s. Reject on any graph inequality that is not a documented extractor limit.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Whole-commit rebuilds for uncommitted work.

recommendations.what: R6. Do not install a Datalog or incremental-maintenance engine now. Revisit when a derived view the agent needs recomputes in over about one second, or the graph or history grows about 100 times. First candidates then: Souffle (UPL, one-shot rules plus provenance explain) or Feldera (MIT, DBSP incremental SQL with recursion). Do not adopt DDlog (archived) or FlowLog (2026 prototype).
recommendations.from_theory: Motik et al.: no clear winner among counting, DRed, FBF; maintenance can lose to rematerialisation; K0 timings show recompute is already microseconds to milliseconds.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids an install that cannot reduce tokens at this size.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: The trigger is a measurement: time recompute of each derived view the agent uses; if any exceeds about one second, run the engine as an arm against recompute and compare answers for equality.
recommendations.needs_install: Only when revisited: souffle-lang/souffle (UPL-1.0, C++/CMake, interpreter mode, packages for Ubuntu/Fedora/Oracle Linux, size not checked) or Feldera (MIT, Docker image; source build about 13 GB of free space); both can run offline on Linux in a container after the first pull.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing.

recommendations.what: R7. Temporal ranking features as ablations only: sweep the recency half-life on co-change weights; add a latest-co-change recency ranker; test time-respecting two-hop co-change chains against static two-hop chains. Check that co-change confidence is not the primary ranker.
recommendations.from_theory: HistoRank (recency beats support and confidence ranking at p=0.04, file proximity best on 6 of 10 systems, confidence worst on all ten); Wu et al. time-respecting paths.
recommendations.expected_effect: Small, a few MAP points at most in the one study.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Tuning commits only, one parameter at a time, paired by commit with intervals; reject if no improvement beyond the interval or if the time-respecting chain does not add recall over the static chain.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: The single recency weight in the co-change layer.

recommendations.what: R8. Make 'does this document citation resolve at this commit' a first-class deterministic fact on doc-to-file and doc-to-identifier edges (the finished test already has missing_ref nodes), and use document hash plus section anchor as premise class D for conclusions that rest on the invariants or handoff documents.
recommendations.from_theory: Context-rot reference check (1.27 percent of references stale, 23 percent of repositories); lineage; Copilot citation check.
recommendations.expected_effect: Catches renamed or removed citation targets without a model; false positives expected (24 percent in the study's 50-sample).
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: Across tuning snapshots, check that every resolution flip after a rename or removal is detected with no false negatives against a full re-resolution; report the false-positive share on a hand-checked sample.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing; extends cites edges.

recommendations.what: R9. Analysis only: classify about 50 findings from existing agent session transcripts into 'expressible as an existing typed query', 'expressible with a new query' and 'interpretation only', and count premises per class.
recommendations.from_theory: Provenance: a claim that is a deterministic query should be stored as a materialised answer revalidated mechanically, leaving only interpretation as model prose.
recommendations.expected_effect: Decides whether the ledger mostly holds free-to-revalidate answers or mostly suspect prose.
recommendations.how_to_test_on_tuning_data: The classification is the test; report counts per class; use transcripts from the tuning period only.
recommendations.replaces_in_current_graph: Nothing.

earlier_research_missed: Second-round lane-temporal.md could not read Build Systems a la Carte; I read it in full. Its early-cutoff note is incomplete: deep constructive traces with two or more levels require deterministic tasks, and non-deterministic tasks relax the correctness definition, which is the basis for the model-conclusion design.

Second-round lane-temporal.md presents a derived conclusion that carries its premises as the build-system idea and 'genuinely new'. It is older and central to provenance (lineage 2001, semirings 2007), truth maintenance (1979, 1986) and incremental view maintenance (1993); those fields document the hard cases build systems handle badly: absence (negation) and alternative derivations.
First-round research listed Souffle and Doop as not covered and did not treat incremental view maintenance, provenance, truth maintenance or incremental computation at all.
First-round table says Glean's Angle is Datalog-like non-recursive; I could not confirm it (Angle intro page does not say; recursion and negation pages returned 404). Treat as unverified.

K0 names its limits well but not the published algorithm behind each part; its negative-dependency patterns are the phantom problem and query-update independence, and its read set is lineage. K0 also ran no static kind-level policy and no exhaustive single-fact mutation test, so its zero-stale result rests on what real history exercised.

The claim that a linear validity interval does not fit a commit DAG is right for Graphiti's model, but the theory that does fit (differential computation over a partial order of versions, McSherry et al. 2013) was not mentioned.

K0's token estimate is correctly caveated, but neither round connects it to the fact that the case for caching rests entirely on model-expensive conclusions, for which the published literature is neutral to negative and which no one has measured on code.
